traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Portulacaceae, which takes in Montiaceae: leaves alternate or opposite; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate or single; blades linear, lanceolate, oblanceolate, ovate or obovate; stipules usually present, rarely absent; plants hermaphrodite; ovary usually superior, rarely half inferior; floral cup present or absent; stems woody or herbaceous; flowers solitary or in cymes; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals or tepals; fruit capsule; stamens 3 to 50; carpels (2-) 3 (-9). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.inflorescence.note: Reed College Montiaceae family sheet (read 2026-10-17): flowers mostly in cymes, sometimes raceme-like, a few solitary. Weighted by genus: Calandrinia s.l. (Wikipedia: 37 spp plus 60-74 Australian species split off as Parakeelya/Rumicastrum, ~100+ together) has cymes; Claytonia (~26-33 spp, SEINet/FNA) has racemose or cymose one-sided clusters. Solitary flowers are the minority.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: Reed College Montiaceae sheet (read 2026-10-17) gives the flowers as radial for the family; Calandrinia (Wikipedia) and Claytonia (SEINet/FNA, five spreading equal petals) are regular. No genus page read shows bilateral flowers, so zygomorphic drops to rarely.

traits.perianth.note: The whole family shares one plan: two green, unequal outer parts and about five showy inner parts. SEINet/FNA Claytonia (read 2026-10-17) and Wikipedia Calandrinia call these sepals and petals; the Reed College sheet reads the outer pair as bracts and the inner as tepals. Drawn, it is a green pair under coloured petals, so sepals and petals leads.

traits.hypanthium.note: Reed College Montiaceae sheet (read 2026-10-17): ovary superior and flowers hypogynous, no floral cup described; neither the Claytonia (SEINet/FNA) nor Calandrinia (Wikipedia) page mentions a cup.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Wikipedia Calandrinia (read 2026-10-17; with the Australian Parakeelya group ~100+ spp, the largest unit): leaves mostly in a basal rosette, alternate or opposite. SEINet/FNA Claytonia (~26-33 spp): basal rosette plus usually one opposite stem pair. Rosettes dominate the big genera, so alternate leads; the lead rests on two genera only, hence often.
